privacy.metaDescription: How TrackDraw handles account, project, sharing, gallery, API, product usage, and operational data.
privacy.effectiveDate: Effective August 16, 2026. This page explains how TrackDraw handles data for accounts, projects, sharing, gallery publishing, embeds, API access, and privacy-safe product analytics.
privacy.s1Body: This Privacy Policy explains how Dutch Drone Squad handles your data when you use trackdraw.app and its hosted features. This policy is intended to be clear and practical, but it is not a substitute for legal advice.
privacy.s2Intro: TrackDraw processes the following categories of information:
privacy.s2Item1: Account information — email address, display name, sign-in state, and authentication metadata.
privacy.s2Item2: Project and track data — layouts, obstacle configurations, project names, and timestamps.
privacy.s2Item3: Sharing and gallery data — share tokens, gallery titles, preview images, and visibility state.
privacy.s2Item4: API data — key metadata, expiry state, and identifiers needed to serve requests.
privacy.s2Item5: Operational and security data — audit logs, authentication events, and error states.
privacy.s2Item6: Product usage data — event type, timestamp, an ephemeral browser-session identifier, and optional account, project, share, or export-format references. This can include a coarse acquisition category such as direct, search, social, community, referral, or campaign, plus categorized operation failures such as validation, authorization, network, storage, or rendering. TrackDraw derives privacy-minimized daily metric counts without browser-session, account, project, or share identifiers, and keeps only the first meaningful-edit timestamp needed for a signed-in creator's 30-day return cohort. To guide interface translations, TrackDraw separately counts creator sessions per day by normalized primary browser language, selected interface locale, and coarse country. The country is derived from Cloudflare request context and immediately aggregated without storing the IP address. Low-volume language and country groups are combined before dashboard disclosure. TrackDraw does not retain the source hostname or raw campaign value in product events. For embedded viewers, TrackDraw separately keeps thresholded daily counts for the published share and referring website hostname. It does not store referring paths or queries, project content, IP addresses, precise location, user-agent strings, device fingerprints, exception messages, or request bodies in product analytics.
privacy.s3Body: TrackDraw uses this information to provide and improve the product, understand aggregate activation and feature usage, prioritize interface translations, show publishers where their embeds are used, protect accounts and the service, and display public content when you choose to publish it. TrackDraw relies on its legitimate interest in operating and improving the hosted service for privacy-safe product analytics and aggregate embed measurement. Language and country counters are not linked to a browser session, account, project, IP address, or track. Referring hostnames are not linked to an embed visitor, browser-session identifier, IP address, or device, are not used for advertising or cross-site profiling, and are shown only to authorized operators and the publisher after at least three detected views. Product analytics, localization-demand aggregates, aggregate embed measurements, and security audit logs are stored separately because they serve different purposes.
privacy.s4Body: If you publish a share or list a track in the gallery, the content and metadata you provide can become public. Unlisted, expired, or revoked links are intended to stay out of search results, but anyone with an active link may still view the shared layout until it expires or is revoked.
privacy.s5Body: TrackDraw uses service providers for hosting, storage, authentication, and email — including Cloudflare for infrastructure. These providers process information only as needed to run TrackDraw and keep the service available. Some operate outside the European Economic Area; where that is the case, TrackDraw relies on standard contractual clauses or other approved transfer mechanisms under applicable data protection law.
privacy.s6Body: TrackDraw uses functional cookies and browser storage for sign-in sessions, theme preference, local projects, editor state, an ephemeral analytics session identifier, and session-scoped deduplication. These are used to operate and improve the application, not to build advertising profiles or track people across sites. TrackDraw does not use analytics or marketing cookies.
privacy.s7Body: Local projects stay on your device until you remove them or clear browser storage. Cloud projects, shares, and account data remain stored until you delete or remove them where the product allows it. Raw product analytics events are removed after 180 days. Privacy-minimized daily product metric and localization-demand counts are removed after 24 months. The account-linked first meaningful-edit timestamp is removed when product analytics is disabled or the account is deleted. Daily aggregate embed-referrer counts are removed after 90 days and are deleted when their published share is deleted. Some operational and security records may be kept for longer when needed to protect the service, comply with legal obligations, or restore reliable operation.
privacy.s8Body: You can use core editing without an account. Product analytics can be disabled below without affecting editing, import, export, sharing, gallery, or read-only use. Anonymous activity is limited to one browser session and is never retrospectively attached after sign-in. A signed-in objection applies on every device and removes account-, project-, and share-linked raw events. Depending on where you live, you may also have rights to access, correct, delete, export, restrict, or object to processing. In the Netherlands, you can complain to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens.
privacy.s9Body: TrackDraw may update this policy when the product or how it handles data changes. Material changes will be reflected here before or when they ship.
privacy.s10Body: For privacy questions or requests, email info@trackdraw.app. Please include "Privacy" in the subject so the message is easier to spot.

terms.metaDescription: Terms for using TrackDraw, including accounts, projects, public shares, gallery publishing, embeds, and API access.
terms.effectiveDate: Effective June 30, 2026. These terms explain the rules for using TrackDraw, including accounts, projects, public sharing, gallery publishing, embeds, and API access.
terms.s1Body: TrackDraw is a browser-based FPV race track design tool. You may use the core editor without an account, and account-backed features are available when you sign in. These Terms apply to trackdraw.app and all hosted TrackDraw features.
terms.s2Body: You are responsible for keeping access to your account, email, passkeys, sessions, and API keys secure. Do not share API keys publicly or use another person's account without permission. TrackDraw may revoke sessions, shares, API keys, or account access when needed to protect the service, investigate abuse, comply with legal obligations, or prevent harm to other users.
terms.s3Body: You keep ownership of the track designs, project data, and other content you create or upload. By saving, publishing, or sharing content through TrackDraw, you give TrackDraw a limited licence to host, process, and deliver that content as needed to provide the service. Do not publish content that you do not have the right to share, that exposes private information without permission, or that is unlawful, abusive, misleading, or harmful.
terms.s4Title: Public shares, gallery listings, and embeds
terms.s4Body1: Published shares, gallery listings, and embeds are intended for read-only review and public or semi-public hand-off. When you list a track in the gallery, its content and metadata may be visible to visitors and search engines. You are responsible for deciding whether a track should be shared publicly.
terms.s4Body2: Do not include private venue details, personal information, or sensitive notes in public content. TrackDraw may hide, unlist, remove, or revoke public content that appears broken, abusive, unlawful, or inconsistent with the product's intended use.
terms.s5Body: API keys are for connecting your own account-backed projects to external tools. You may not use the API to overload the service, bypass access controls, scrape private data, or interfere with other users. External integrations are your responsibility, and TrackDraw may change, limit, or revoke API access when needed for security, reliability, compatibility, or abuse prevention.
terms.s6Body: TrackDraw exports and outputs are planning aids. You are responsible for verifying the real venue, race rules, safety constraints, and final build before use. Experimental outputs may require manual review and adjustment before they are suitable for an event.
terms.s7Body: TrackDraw's source code is available under the AGPL-3.0-only license so the community can inspect, learn from, and contribute to the project. The hosted service at trackdraw.app is separate from the source code. Hosted features depend on third-party services and may be limited, changed, suspended, or offered under paid plans in the future. TrackDraw is provided as-is; features may be updated, limited, paused, or removed, and hosted services may be interrupted by maintenance, infrastructure issues, or provider outages.
terms.s8Body: TrackDraw does not promise that any output, export, integration, or shared content will be accurate, available, or suitable for every use case. To the maximum extent allowed by applicable law, TrackDraw is not liable for indirect, incidental, or consequential damages, or for loss of data, event disruption, or safety issues arising from use of the service.
terms.s9Body: TrackDraw may update these Terms when the product or legal requirements change. Continued use after changes means you accept the updated Terms.
terms.s10Body: For questions about these Terms, email info@trackdraw.app. Please include "Terms" in the subject so the message is easier to spot.
